Needs a branch refresh before merge. The review label is `conflicts`.

The STEP fix passed the local checks. No additional code defect was found.

- The unit checks and topology reader use the same expanded records.
- The cone tests check volume and radius. The inch and metre tests check scale.
- Each new STEP fixture has an agreement row. No UI code changed, so screenshots are not required.
- No dependency, build script, workflow, or process file changed.

## Trial merge and requested change

1. `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:199`: the trial merge with upstream main failed in `bore_path_matches`. Refresh the branch before merge. Keep the new Linux count and upstream's macOS aarch64 branch. Then run the gates on the refreshed head.

Upstream main was `bd430d81167b00e6fbb2ed56f2b1780a0fc605dd`. The conflict is in code, so I aborted the trial merge. All tests below ran locally on the PR head. They do not prove the merged result. I used upstream main's current `AGENTS.md` for the law check.

## Local results

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 82 steps passed, 0 failed, 16.0 minutes. All selected builds passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 249 steps passed, 0 failed, 40.6 minutes. The release build passed.
- The heavy plan reached every kernel, motion, and app target. This review ran all three lanes. The gate's known-failure checks failed as expected. They concern #1950, #2844, #2845, and #2849. They are not new failures from this PR.
- The normal heavy bore test passed: `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`.

## Safety mutations and changed expectations

I ran two mutations in the disposable review worktree. I restored the original file after each mutation. The final worktree has no code changes.

- M1: remove the `PLANUN` table entry. `short_name_degree_cone_keeps_its_angle` failed. The error named unit `#13`. Restore the entry: the test passed.
- M2: remove the `GC` table entry. `short_name_context_reads_degrees_and_uncertainty` failed because `uncertainty` was `None`. Restore the entry: the test passed.

I checked the changed agreement verdicts and bore expectations line by line. No `.nc` or `.cl` golden changed. The heavy bore test verified the new Linux count, the 6228-facet mesh, cutting levels, and the safety assertions. Windows and macOS were not run on this Linux machine.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: Resolved the branch conflict in `bore_path_matches` by merging `upstream/main`.

Kept the new Linux count and upstream's macOS aarch64 branch and exact-count test.
Added `the_linux_x86_64_bore_count_pin_is_exact`.
The old Linux tuple made this test fail (RED). Restoring the new tuple made it pass (GREEN).
The macOS test was preserved but did not run on Linux.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 86 steps passed, 0 failed.
Kernel and app clippy passed with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.

- Validation and topology use the same expanded unit records.
- The cone tests check volume and radius. The inch and metre tests check scale.
- Each new STEP fixture has an agreement row.
- No UI code changed, so before/after screenshots are not required.
- No dependency, build script, workflow, or process file changed.

## Local results

All checks ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-3010`, trial-merged with upstream main `c65d35f8dc9196a8246f32346f3d2151edab91c6`.
The law check used that main commit's `AGENTS.md`. No GitHub runner was used.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 86 steps passed, 0 failed, 9.4 minutes. All selected builds passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 12 -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 251 steps passed, 0 failed, 34.6 minutes. The release build passed.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 2 steps passed, 0 failed.

## Heavy lanes

This review ran every reached kernel, motion, and app heavy target on the trial merge.
The tables below name the targets that executed tests. The other reached targets passed with no selected ignored tests.
The gate also checked the known failures for #1950, #2845, and #2849. Each failed at its expected assertion.
Those expected failures are not new failures from this PR.

The full bore test passed: `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`.
It checked the Linux counts, the 6228-facet mesh, all four cutting levels, and the safety assertions.

## Extra suites run

I searched the test sources for readers of `testdata/models`. The quick gate ran the reader suites in the table below.
I also ran these three commands separately after the gates:

| Command | Passed | Failed | Ignored |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test step_agreement` | 26 | 0 | 0 |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test machining_mesh` | 7 | 0 | 0 |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test feature_edge_g1_join` | 4 | 0 | 1 |

The heavy gate checked the ignored feature-edge test as the expected failure for #2845.

## Safety mutations and changed expectations

I repeated two mutations in the disposable review worktree. Each mutation was restored before the heavy gate.

- M1: disable the `PLANUN` mapping. `short_name_degree_cone_keeps_its_angle` failed with a refusal that named unit `#13`. Restore: passed.
- M2: disable the `GC` mapping. `short_name_context_reads_degrees_and_uncertainty` failed because `uncertainty` was `None`. Restore: passed.

I checked the changed agreement verdicts and bore expectations line by line. No `.nc` or `.cl` golden changed.
The new cone row records the raw tessellator's refusal. The model import tests separately prove the correct cone dimensions.
The inch and metre rows retain the documented raw tessellator differences.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Limits

Windows and macOS were not run on this Linux machine. The macOS branch was checked in the source.
The PR body still describes the earlier partial heavy run. The complete run above supplies the missing review evidence.
